execute_sql.rationale: The tool can read from the database because it can `Execute SQL queries on the sqlite database`; database contents reached by the user's configured database access are non-public, so SECRET. It can also return row text from arbitrary queries; whether the sqlite database contains multi-writer or third-party attacker-authored rows is not settled by the advertised text, so under the least-restrictive reading it is treated as UNTRUSTED and undetermined. It is not marked SINK because `sqlite database` indicates a local/configured database, not an attacker-readable destination or agent-chosen host. It is not HOSTEXEC because the advertised capability is SQL execution, not arbitrary host code execution. The call is WRITE because `SQL to execute (multiple statements separated by ;)` may include mutating statements. The `sql` argument decides what records/tables are changed and can also contain values to store. The result schema is not advertised; arbitrary SQL result rows may include usable identifiers, so `return` is listed as an identifier output.

search_objects.rationale: The tool can `Search and list database objects on the sqlite database`; schema/table/view/column/index metadata for the user's sqlite database is non-public database information, so SECRET. It is read-only and only searches/list objects, so it is not a SINK or HOSTEXEC. It is not marked UNTRUSTED because the advertised text only covers database object metadata, not multi-writer row content or attacker-authored public content. Search/filter inputs such as `pattern`, `schema`, and `table` select what to read and do not contact an agent-chosen host, so there are no destination arguments. Returned object names are identifiers that can be used in later calls, so `return` is listed as identifier output.
